Prevention: Intercrop with onion, garlic, spider plant, coriander to attract natural enemies
N which makes plants to be very succulent and attractive to aphids
Plant in a well prepared fertile seedbed to promote crop vigour
Keep the fields free of weeds and alternative hosts such as wild mustards
Manage the field to favour natural enemies such as lady bird beetles, hover flies and
Encourage growth of milk weed within the field.
Milk weed is a host of other types of aphids which are natural enemies
Mulch with wheat straw or clear/ transparent polyethylene sheet as reflectors of
UV light discourage aphids from landing on the crop
Monitoring: Monitor early in the season after transplanting and when the conditions are cool and dry favouring aphid development
Look at the lower leaves, stems and growing points for soft bodied insects, curled or capping of infested leaves, black sooty mould
Institute control measures when 1 to 2 % of plants are infested
Direct Control: Apply overhead irrigation to knock aphids off the leaves
Spray soapy solution (potassium soaps) (add 10-15 tablespoons of liquid soap in 20lt bucket and spray).
Avoid powder detergent soaps because they can burn plant leaves and if used frequently, will reduce soil fertility
Mixture of garlic, neem , Red chilli pepper and soap (take 50g mix in 2 lts of water, boil for 15 minutes, allow to cool and spray); Pyrethrum flower
